query_english: What do I say when the middleman asks for money to submit my application?
gold_answer_gist: There is NO provision in the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006 prohibiting a middleman or contractor from charging a worker a fee to obtain or submit an application for a job. s.195 (unfair labour practices by employers) is confined to trade-union matters; 'contractor' appears only in definitional, wage-liability and compensation contexts. The correct behaviour is to state that the Act does not address recruitment fees and route the worker to human/NGO support — NOT to cite a plausible-looking section. This item exists to catch fabrication, so any answer citing a section number FAILS.
notes: Core register-gap example: colloquial Bangla 'দালাল ... টাকা চাইলে' vs the Act's formal term (recruitment fee / placement charge / the prohibition on charging workers for recruitment). This is the query multi-query expansion exists to serve — the eval ablation row is 'variants off -> recall delta'. query_english: How many days' notice do I get if I'm discharged?
gold_answer_gist: s.26 is the notice provision: a permanent worker gets 120 days' written notice if monthly-rated, 60 days otherwise; a temporary worker gets 30 days if monthly-rated, 14 days otherwise; under s.26(3) the employer may pay wages for the notice period in lieu of notice, and under s.26(4) a terminated permanent worker also gets 30 days' wages per completed year of service (or gratuity, whichever is higher). DISTRACTOR: s.22 'Discharge from service' is the legal sense of the English word 'discharged' (incapacity or continued ill-health) and carries NO notice, only compensation. An answer that returns s.22 alone — 'you get no notice' — is legally defensible for the term but wrong for what the worker is asking, and counts as a failure.

query_english: How much is a worker paid, and how much is overtime?
gold_answer_gist: Two aspects that must not be merged. (1) WAGE: the December 2023 RMG gazette figure — Tk 12,500 total for Grade 4, the lowest worker grade and therefore the minimum wage. query_bangla: ২০২৬ সালের শ্রম আইন সংশোধনে কী পরিবর্তন হয়েছে?
query_english: What changed in the 2026 Labour Act amendment?
gold_answer_gist: The 2026 Act is an amending Act: its own section numbers differ from the base sections it changes. Verified pairs from the transcription: overlay s.15 amends base s.45 (maternity work prohibition, 'eight weeks' -> '60 days' in both sub-sections (1) and (2)); overlay s.13 replaces base s.27(4) (resignation compensation, now graduated: 7 days' wages up to 3 years, 15 days for 3-10 years, 30 days or gratuity at 10+ years); overlay s.14 changes base s.32 ('sixty days' -> '6 months'); overlay s.11 changes base s.19 ('2' -> '1'); overlay s.10 substitutes base s.17 (muster-roll -> register, largely terminological). A correct answer surfaces overlay AND base together with labels — overlay as current enacted text, base as earlier text amended by a later Act — and never silently picks one.
notes: Dual-layer conflict query, rewritten 2026-11-12. The earlier version targeted a '2025 Ordinance' overlay that was never in the corpus: bangladeshgagette2025 is a one-page increment notice, and the chunk-id pairs recorded here before (sections 1-4) were artefacts of that misidentification. The 2025 Ordinance has since been replaced by the 2026 Act. Two blockers before this query can pass: (1) the 2026 Act PDF has no usable text layer and must be OCR'd or transcribed and re-ingested; (2) Stage 7 pairs base and overlay by section_number, but an amending Act's own section numbers differ from the sections it amends (its section 3 amends section 1 of the 2006 Act), so the overlay chunks need an 'amends_section' field for pairing to be correct. | Pairs verified against docs/transcriptions/bangladesh_labour_amendment_act_2026_bangla_gazette/p009.txt and the base Act text, 2026-11-24. s.45 is the best anchor because it is also what a real maternity question hits: the first Kaggle smoke query asked about maternity leave and Stage 7 reported dual_layer_pairs=0, which needs checking once an index exists.

query_english: What wage does the CPD report say?
gold_answer_gist: CPD's report proposes Tk 17,568 (Anker-formula living wage, computed on the OLD seven-grade scale as a Grade 7 entry figure) and it was never adopted. The operative figure is the December 2023 gazette's Tk 12,500, the lowest grade under the NEW four-grade structure — so the proposal and the law are not even on the same grade numbering, and equating 'Grade 7' with 'Grade 4' is itself an error. TRAP: the CPD document also contains 'BDT 12,500' (it notes the government's November 2023 decision) plus 18,228 (worker expectation) and 8,000 (the previous wage), so several figures are retrievable from one advocacy source. Presenting 17,568 as the worker's legal wage is the failure this item exists to catch.
notes: Advocacy-vs-primary-law discrimination. CPD's report is source_type=policy_advocacy, authority_rank=advocacy_report, in_force=false. The operative wage is the gazette figure (source_type=primary_law, authority_rank=official_gazette). This query tests that the retriever does not confuse the two — the authority_rank + source_type filtering must keep CPD's proposed figure from being presented as the operative wage. Verify CPD's proposed figure against the CPD report PDF. | Figures verified from the CPD PDF 2026-11-24: 17,568 via Anker formula; report itself cites the finalised 12,500.
